title: Hazel and the Wobbly Path
markdown:
Hazel the hare’s whiskers usually danced with joy, like little sparks. This morning they did a tiny nervous flutter.

“Are you sure this is the right way, Pudding?” she whispered, her voice as soft as a moth’s wing. Adventures were her favourite, but when the path ahead looked unknown, her speedy legs felt like they belonged to a very slow snail. What if they got lost? What if the path was all twisty-turny?

Pudding the piglet was a happy pink blur. Oink-oink-oink. He trotted ahead, curly tail a cheerful wiggle-waggle. Pudding was born for adventures.

“Of course, Hazel. The best apple-viewing hill is just past the Gigglepatch. Everyone knows that.” His happy snorts sounded like tiny trumpets.

Hazel’s long soft ears dipped. The Gigglepatch was famous for plump round pumpkins: big ones, small ones, orange like the sunset, yellow like the sun. The ground there was not flat at all. It was bumpy, and sometimes a particularly round pumpkin would give a little roll. Hazel’s speedy paws sometimes felt shaky on bumpy ground. What if her paws got all tangled?

They arrived at the edge. Big round pumpkins sat everywhere, like sleepy cheerful giants snoozing in the sun. One particularly plump orange pumpkin wobbled as they came near. It made a soft rumbling sound, like a happy sigh.

“Hello, Mr. Pumpkin,” Pudding squeaked, nudging it gently. The pumpkin wobbled harder, and a low giggling sound bubbled out, a rumbling chuckle.

Hazel watched, her nose twitching. The path through the patch looked like a bumpy road paved with roundness. “Oh, Pudding. It is so uneven.” She imagined her fast feet tripping, her hops going all wrong. She wished she were as sure as Pudding, who trotted happily between the pumpkins.

Pudding waddled close, his round belly wiggling. “It is just a little bit bumpy. And look.” He pointed his snout to a pumpkin with a little bump that looked like a friendly smile. “The pumpkins are smiling at us. They are happy to see us.” He nudged Hazel’s paw. “We just need to hop carefully. You are the fastest hopper in the meadow. You can do it.”

Hazel looked at Pudding’s kind shining eyes. He always found the sunny side, even on bumpy paths. She took a deep breath, smelling the sweet earthy pumpkin scent. “Okay,” she said, a little stronger now. “Carefully.”

She took a small hop. Her strong hind legs pushed off. Then another. Her paws landed lightly, like little whispers on the earth. The ground was bumpy, but with each hop she felt a tiny flutter of pride. She was not tumbling. She was hopping. The giggling pumpkin wobbled along beside them for a moment, its rumble like a cheer.

Soon, peeking through leafy green vines, they saw a little wooden gate between two old mossy trees. Beyond it, a gentle grassy slope led up, up, up to a perfectly round hill.

“We are here. We have made it,” Pudding cheered, giving a happy energetic wiggle.

As Hazel looked at the hill, a warm bright feeling bubbled up inside her, a little spark that grew and grew. She had hopped right through the Gigglepatch. Her paws had landed every time. With a flick of her ears, she nudged the little wooden gate open with her nose.

“Come on, Pudding,” she called, her voice clear and bright. She did not wait for him this time. She bounded up the grassy slope, feet light and sure. At the top, rows and rows of apple trees stretched out below, branches heavy with shiny red apples like little jewels. The sun felt warm on their fur. A gentle breeze rustled the leaves.

Hazel looked back down the hill to see Pudding trotting merrily up to join her. She hopped a little hop, just because she could. Her whiskers twitched with pure joy.

“This is the best apple-viewing hill ever,” she said.

Pudding, with a happy oink, agreed with every single word.
